sections.text: Thirteen trials test CD19 CAR-T in myasthenia gravis (MG), with 11 currently running, one stopped before enrollment, and one with unknown status.
Among running trials, there is one Phase 2/3 trial (NCT06193889), one Phase 1/2 trial (NCT06359041), and nine Phase 1 or early Phase 1 trials.
Sponsors of active trials include Cabaletta Bio, Kyverna, BMS, Kite, TG Therapeutics, Zhejiang University, and several academic or hospital-based investigators.
One trial (NCT06419166) was withdrawn before enrolling any participants due to the study stopping early.

A 2026 case series in Cell Reports Medicine (PMID:42628528) reported three patients with refractory MG achieving sustained clinical remission for at least 19 months after anti-CD19 CAR T-cell therapy, allowing discontinuation of other immunotherapies.
Recent reviews from 2026 (e.g., PMID:42936601, PMID:42824951) describe CD19 CAR-T as a promising strategy for deep and durable B-cell depletion in autoimmune neurologic diseases including MG.
The site's stop-risk model estimates a median 22.3% risk of termination across eight running CD19 CAR-T trials in MG, based on design and enrollment factors.
CD19 CAR-T is being explored alongside other advanced cellular and biologic therapies for MG, but early clinical data suggest potential for durable, treatment-free remission in refractory cases.

read: Mechanism evidence: Early clinical data support durable remission in refractory MG after CD19 CAR-T therapy.
Competitive position: Multiple companies and academic centers are advancing CD19 CAR-T in MG, with a modest estimated stop risk of 22.3%.
Open questions: Long-term safety, durability beyond two years, and optimal patient selection remain uncertain.
would_change: New safety signals from ongoing trials would shift the stance to mixed or against.
Failure of the Phase 2/3 KYV-101 trial (NCT06193889) to show efficacy would weaken the evidence base.
